thread:
maya: FYI rolled gpu-operator 1.13 to us-west-2 at 10:08 and started seeing pods with gpu requests Pending with 'no nodes available' :eyes:
deploy-bot: rollout gpu-operator v1.13 -> v1.13 across us-west-2 finished (canary -> 80%)
jules: seeing the same in staging earlier, thought it was a config drift. attaching kube-scheduler logs snippet:
```
I0315 10:12:44.123 scheduler.go:554] Pod default/train-abc: unschedulable: 0/120 nodes are available: 112 node(s) didn't match Pod's nodeSelector, 8 node(s) had insufficient nvidia.com/gpu resources.
```
sam: quick check - device-plugin changed advertised resource name during upgrade? our NodeAffinity rules pin to `nvidia.com/gpu` resource label currently.
liam: confirmed: new plugin advertises `nvidia.com/gpu.present=true` and adds node annotation `gpu.vendor/nvidia=true` instead of increasing `capacity` field. looks like a discovery-label flip.
maya: oof, that would break any Fit predicate looking at capacity. we need either to patch the plugin or update schedulers fast. Can we hotfix? :hammer:
jules: suggest patching the device-plugin DaemonSet to preserve `capacity` advertise by setting ENV DISCOVER_MODE=legacy (if available). quick command I ran in staging:
```
kubectl -n gpu-operators set env ds/nvidia-device-plugin DISCOVER_MODE=legacy
kubectl -n gpu-operators rollout restart ds/nvidia-device-plugin
```
liam: after doing that in staging pods started scheduling again. but for prod nodes already marked `Allocatable` with zero gpus in some kubelets. we need a rolling kubelet restart on affected nodes to pick up capacity change.
oncall-sre: I'm oncall, will coordinate. how many nodes impacted in us-west-2?
maya: ~24 A100 nodes in pool gpu-prod-west reported below allocatable yesterday after the upgrade. draining that many will impact throughput for queued jobs.
sam: cost/impact note: if we evict and reschedule to other pools it'll push up preemptible usage and burn reserved capacity on dedicated clusters. estimate +15% token-cost for the week if we move traffic.
jules: plan options:
- revert gpu-operator in region to 1.12 (fast rollback)
- patch device-plugin env to advertise legacy resource and restart kubelets gradually
- update our workload PodSpecs to tolerate new annotation and use nodeSelector by annotation (risky)
maya: I prefer rollback the operator release for minimal application change. can infra do rollback and hold canary?
oncall-sre: I can trigger rollback. need an approver for prod rollback outside of normal change window. tagging sam and liam for sign-off. @sam @liam
sam: 👍 we should roll back the operator in us-west-2 to 1.12 and pause further upgrades. also open a ticket to add an integration test ensuring device-plugin preserves capacity fields.
liam: +1. I'll prepare the rollback job and a small patch to device-plugin that re-adds capacity advertise for later safe re-upgrade.
maya: I'm going to notify customers using Dedicated capacity in us-west-2 with a short note. I'll mention possible brief scheduling interruptions but outline rollback in progress.
oncall-sre: Rolling back now (command):
```
kubectl -n gpu-operators set image deployment/gpu-operator gpu-operator=redwood/gpu-operator:v1.12.4
kubectl -n gpu-operators rollout status deployment/gpu-operator
```
deploy-bot: rollback job started for us-west-2 by oncall-sre at 10:32, monitoring for completions.
jules: after rollback let's run this verification checklist:
- ensure Node allocatable shows gpu count (kubectl describe node <node> | grep Allocatable)
- start tiny gpu pod with `resources.limits.nvidia.com/gpu: 1` and ensure it schedules
- run short NCCL smoke test across 2 nodes to confirm no runtime mismatch
maya: adding runbook entry to infra.incidents and tagging eng-sre. also opened ticket INFRA-4291 to track permanent fix.
sam: thanks team. keep thread updated as rollback completes. if we still see nodes stuck with zero-gpu allocatable after rollback, we will need kubelet restarts + node restart window. :clock1:
